verdicts.title: resetAmount rebases startTime to now, so claiming 0 locked tokens skips the vesting delay at no cost

a.reden: The candidate describes a startTime rebasing issue in resetAmount, which is not covered by any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes a startTime rebasing flaw in resetAmount, which is a different root cause and impact from the known findings, including M-5's double-spending issue in resetVestingPlans.

verdicts.title: Reset check compares new amount to old unlocked amount, so addLiquidity reverts for users with an existing LP plan

a.reden: Both describe the same faulty check in Vesting.sol::_resetVestingPlans that blocks adding liquidity after unlocked tokens exceed the new amount

b.reden: The candidate describes the same flawed `_resetVestingPlans` check that prevents adding liquidity in `SymmVesting`.

verdicts.title: Permissionless notifyRewardAmount lets anyone stretch the reward period and lose rewards to rounding

a.reden: Both describe the permissionless notifyRewardAmount allowing anyone to extend the reward period and dilute rewards

b.reden: Both describe that anyone can call notifyRewardAmount with tiny amounts to extend the reward period, diluting rewards.

a.reden: Both describe the same flaw where re‑adding a previously delisted reward token leaves perTokenStored non‑zero and userRewardPerTokenPaid unsynced, letting users who deposited during the delisted perio

b.reden: Both describe the same root cause: users who stake while a reward token is delisted keep userRewardPerTokenPaid at 0, and re-adding the token without resetting perTokenStored lets them claim historica

verdicts.title: rewardPerToken floors per update and lastUpdated always advances, so frequent updates destroy rewards for low-decimal tokens

a.reden: Both describe the same flooring loss in rewardPerToken/_updateRewardsStates causing USDC rewards to be lost when updates are frequent.

b.reden: Both describe loss of rewards due to integer truncation in rewardPerToken when updates are frequent, especially for low-decimal tokens like USDC.

verdicts.title: Rewards accrued while totalSupply is 0 are lost and block delisting of the reward token

a.reden: The candidate describes a distinct issue with rewards lost when totalSupply is zero and token delisting, which does not correspond to any listed known finding.

b.reden: The candidate describes lost rewards during zero totalSupply and blocked token removal, which is a different root cause from the known findings.

verdicts.title: Reset or locked claim on a fully vested plan reverts, and a finished plan cannot be re-setup

a.reden: The candidate describes a different revert logic for finished vesting plans, not the bad check described in M-3 or any other known finding.

b.reden: The candidate describes a different root cause (resetAmount reverting on finished plans and setup blocking re-setup) than the known findings, which concern reward accounting, initialization, reset che

verdicts.title: resetVestingPlans bounds the new amount by already-claimed tokens, and resetAmount drops claim history

a.reden: Both describe resetAmount resetting claimedAmount to zero, allowing re‑granting of already‑claimed tokens and causing double‑spending.

b.reden: Both describe resetAmount resetting claimedAmount to zero after a claimed-amount check, allowing already-claimed tokens to be re-granted/double spent.

verdicts.title: A single reverting reward token blocks claimRewards for all reward tokens

a.reden: The candidate describes a different issue (reverting token blocking all claims) not covered by any known finding.

b.reden: The candidate describes a reverting reward token blocking all claims, which is not the same root cause as any listed known finding.

verdicts.title: totalVested[SYMM] is not reduced when locked SYMM is moved into the pool by addLiquidity

a.reden: The candidate describes a different issue (totalVested not decremented) not covered by any known finding.

b.reden: The candidate describes a totalVested accounting error in _addLiquidityProcess, which is not the same root cause as any listed finding.

verdicts.title: Setter can re-allocate users who already claimed, enabling a second mint

a.reden: The candidate describes a reallocation bug in SymmAllocationClaimer.sol, which is not covered by any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate concerns SymmAllocationClaimer's setBatchAllocations/claim reallocation, while none of the known findings describe that contract or root cause.

verdicts.title: addLiquidity default USDC and LP slippage checks give no protection against pool manipulation

a.reden: The candidate describes a slippage check manipulation in addLiquidity, which does not correspond to any listed known finding.

b.reden: The candidate describes a different vulnerability in addLiquidity slippage checks, not present in the known findings.

verdicts.title: Reward-rate truncation leaves unclaimable dust in pendingRewards, so delisting can never pass the <=10 check

a.reden: The candidate describes reward-rate truncation causing unclaimable dust, which is a different root cause than any listed findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes rate-flooring dust that blocks reward-token delisting, not the known H-1 issue of frequent _updateRewardsStates causing USDC rewards not to distribute.

verdicts.title: AirdropHelper final batch deletes entire arrays and can run out of gas on large airdrops

a.reden: The candidate describes an unbounded array deletion gas issue in AirdropHelper, which does not correspond to any listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate concerns unbounded array deletion in AirdropHelper, while all known findings are unrelated issues in SymmStaking/Vesting contracts.
